examples.knowledge_point: Negating a Sentence Containing a Disjunction
examples.problem:
What is the negation of the following compound statement?

$\qquad$ $3$ is not prime or $\pi$ is not rational.
examples.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

$$
\neg ( A \lor B) = \neg A \land \neg B.
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(3\text{ is not prime}\text{ or }\pi \text{ is not rational}) & ≡¬((3\text{ is not prime})∨(\pi \text{ is not rational})) \\  & ≡¬(3\text{ is not prime})∧¬(\pi \text{ is not rational}) \\  & ≡(3\text{ is prime})∧(\pi \text{ is rational}) \\  & ≡3\text{ is prime}\text{ and }\pi \text{ is rational}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
$\,$ $0$ is not positive and $0$ is not negative.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
feedback.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

$$
¬(A∧B)=¬A∨¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,¬(0\text{ is not positive}\text{ and }0\text{ is not negative}) & ≡¬((0\text{ is not positive})∧(0\text{ is not negative})) \\  & ≡¬(0\text{ is not positive})∨¬(0\text{ is not negative}) \\  & ≡(0\text{ is positive})∨(0\text{ is negative}) \\  & ≡0\text{ is positive}\text{ or }0\text{ is negative}.\end{aligned}
$$
